$comment: PUBLICATION ALLOWLIST. This file is the only thing that decides what reaches the public site.
The build never walks a directory looking for documents to publish. It reads this list and
nothing else. A document that is not listed here cannot be published, and a document listed
with "publish": false is imported for link resolution but is never rendered or copied.
Two consequences worth stating plainly:
1. Adding a page to the public site is always a reviewable diff to this file.
2. Analysis that lives outside the three repositories - for example the Pond Protocol
strategy notes held in the private agent store - has no path onto the site at all.
scripts/guard.mjs additionally fails the build if such material shows up in the output.
See site/README.md for the reasoning and scripts/guard.mjs for the enforced invariants.

$comment: Direct links to the real $PND, rendered into /verify/ by the {{canonicalLinks}} placeholder.
Why this list is load-bearing rather than a convenience. On at least one major XRPL trading
front-end, having a token page is not the same as being findable: a token with a $649k market
cap and roughly 63,000 holders was verified on 2026-09-15 to have a working page that could
not be reached by searching either its ticker or its issuer address - the address search
returned no results and the ticker search surfaced only sub-$300 tokens instead. It was
reachable only by direct URL. That is not a small-token artifact, so a user who cannot find
$PND by searching has no reliable path to it except a link from a source they already trust.
Publishing these links is therefore the primary anti-impersonation mitigation, not the
issuer address alone.
Every entry has a status:
unverified - the URL is derived from a documented or observed route shape but nobody has
loaded it. Rendered with a visible warning. This is the correct state for
anything that depends on $PND existing, because it does not exist yet.
verified   - somebody loaded it in a browser and it rendered the right token. Set the
verifiedOn date at the same time.
Do not promote anything to verified without loading it. A confidently-presented dead link is
worse than an absent one: it teaches readers that this page's links cannot be trusted, which
is the one thing the page depends on.

$comment: Filesystem roots the sync step may read. Any path resolving outside these roots is rejected.
`ref` says WHICH VERSION of each document gets vendored, and it is load-bearing:
"worktree"  read the file from disk as checked out. Correct for this repository, whose
documents are edited in the same commit as the site.
<git ref>   read via `git show <ref>:<path>`. Correct for sibling repositories, because it
pins exactly what was vendored instead of depending on whatever happens to be
checked out on the machine that ran sync.
`pinnedReason` is REQUIRED whenever `ref` is not "main" or "worktree". A pin means this site
is vendoring documentation from an unmerged branch, which is a temporary state that must be
visible rather than discovered later. The build prints a warning for every pin, the guard
fails if a pin has no reason, and `sync --check` fails once the pinned branch has merged.
There are no pins right now. `pnd` was pinned to its correction branch while PND PR #3 was
open, because pnd/main still presented Default Ripple as enabled on an issuer whose Flags are
0. That PR has merged, so all three sources read from their default branch again.
